criteria.criterion: F1: the design drops the claim that disjoint change jobs land through local replay. It states that each job lands through its own pull request by squash, and that Athena rebuilds the local branch on the merged commit after each landing. It cites docs/design/native-pr-landing.md. It says what happens to a job whose base is behind the new HEAD, and §7, the open question on plan, and the build order (§10) are rewritten to match.
criteria.evidence: Section 7 opens with 'What this revision drops' and explains that replay works only over records-only changes. I read land.rs lines 55-74 and they confirm this. Section 7 then says landing goes through a per-job pull request by squash, followed by resync_onto_merge, and cites native-pr-landing.md §5.2a. Point 3 covers a job whose base is behind the new HEAD in four cases: records-only replay, stale, merged-unverified, and re-verify on request (§5.7). Question 2 in section 11 is settled to match, and section 10 step 3 puts settling the landing mechanism before the pool.

criteria.criterion: F2: the design recommends one child process per job as the default. It lists why threads are not chosen (AgentDriver and Ui have no Send/Sync bound, a caught panic is not enough isolation) and says what a spike would have to show to restore threads. The process model covers how the launcher spawns workers, collects results and exit codes, and handles the kill switch.
criteria.evidence: Section 4.1 recommends A (one child process per job). Under B it gives three reasons threads are not chosen: no Send/Sync bound on AgentDriver (agent lib.rs:139) or Ui (core lib.rs:56), a caught panic is not enough isolation, and RefCell at run.rs:1128. I confirmed all three locations with Grep. The section also lists four spike conditions that would have to hold to bring threads back. Section 4.2 covers spawning, piped output, mapping exit status to a result, and the kill switch.

criteria.criterion: F3: a section on shared append-only files (CHANGELOG.md, docs/decisions.md numbering, README.md) states concrete rules. These cover which job writes them, how number allocation avoids two jobs taking the same number, how the pool serializes jobs that name the same file, and what a collision test must check. It says which of these the landing check enforces and which are only hints.
criteria.evidence: Section 9 states four rules: only a docs job that runs alone writes these files; that docs job allocates numbers at write time from the tip; jobs whose briefs name the same file are serialized; and the landing check is the authority. It also includes a table of what is enforced versus what is only a hint, a four-point collision test, and a statement of the root cause.

summary: The revised parallel-jobs design passes all six criteria. It answers review findings F1 to F8 and builds on native pull-request landing: each job lands through its own pull request by squash, and the local branch is rebuilt after each landing. It drops the earlier claim that independent jobs would land by being replayed locally. A job whose base has fallen behind ends stale and is re-checked only when the user asks. The design recommends one child process per job, gives the reasons threads were not chosen, and says what a test spike would have to show to bring them back. A new section 9 sets rules for CHANGELOG.md, decision numbering and README.md, says which rules the landing check enforces and which are only hints, and describes a collision test. I checked the line references against the source with Grep and they are accurate, including run.rs lines 111, 116, 698, 1165, 1178, 1344 and 1424 and land.rs lines 55-81. Besides the design, only CHANGELOG.md and roadmap.md changed, and both edits are small. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo test` both pass. My only findings are a nit and a minor one, and both gaps are disclosed in the document.
